sections.html:
Gahanna is a Columbus suburb with its own school district and its own downtown on the creek. The city lies in Franklin County and shares borders with Columbus on three sides, New Albany to the north, and Mifflin and Jefferson townships. A few small islands of Jefferson Township sit inside the city limits, so ask the Franklin County Auditor which taxing districts apply to your parcel.

Big Walnut Creek, with its tributaries Rocky Fork Creek and Sycamore Run, still shapes the map. Three practical items come up for sellers here: how rental registration affects a landlord's sale, what the county charges to transfer title, and how the creeks bear on a parcel.

The population is 35,986 for July 1, 2025, up 0.7 percent from the 2020 count of 35,726. Seven in ten households own their home, and the median owner-occupied value is $350,900.

  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 14,254
  • Owner-occupied share of housing: 70.6%
  • Median gross rent: $1,466
  • Median household income: $109,061
  • Mean commute: 20.4 minutes

Households average 2.47 people, so a listing that shows a workable home office and room for children speaks to the people who live here.

A buyer who keeps the property as a rental must register it within 30 days of the transfer. Gahanna's Ordinance 0053-2018 requires every residential rental owner to register every two years.

  • Registration runs between January 1 and March 15, and approved permits expire December 31 of the second year.
  • Inspectors check the exterior from the sidewalk or right-of-way against the city codes and the International Property Maintenance Code, and no one has to be home.
  • Owner-occupied single-family homes (occupied more than half the year) may request an exemption case by case.
  • Airbnb-style rentals under 30 consecutive days count as short-term rentals and fall under the same program.

If tenants are in place when you sell, ask Code Enforcement whether any violations are open on the permit, since an unresolved report can slow a buyer's lender.

sections.h2: Preparing a Gahanna house for a buyer
sections.html:
Buyers in a market with strong incomes expect a tidy inspection report. Before you list, walk the property for the items the city codes cover: exterior condition, yard debris, parking and any posted notice. Fix what you can and keep receipts. If a city notice is open, ask Code Enforcement how to close it out, because an unresolved report can slow a buyer's lender.

Gather the deed, the latest tax bill and the state disclosure form. Landlords should add the lease and the registration paperwork. If an owner has died, bring whatever proves who may sign. These are the first things a title company asks for, and having them ready keeps the days between contract and closing short.

The Franklin County Auditor bills $3 per $1,000 of price on a standard sale, split between a $1 state share and a $2 county share, and adds a $0.50 transfer tax. Use the Auditor's online calculator, which asks you to round the price up to the next $100 and applies a $3 floor.

The county share is waived when the seller holds the homestead exemption on the transfer date, which cuts the rate to $1 per $1,000. An exempt conveyance owes just the $0.50. The calculator accepts cash, business checks and cashier's checks payable to the Franklin County Auditor and turns away personal checks, and the amount must be exact.

ORC 319.202 puts the statement of value on the buyer's side and makes the seller pay the fee. Value includes any mortgage or lien. The Transfer and Conveyance department answers questions at 614-525-3253.

Check your homestead exemption before closing. The standard credit goes to owners aged 65 by year-end or permanently and totally disabled, within an income cap. Owners who are 100 percent disabled through military service can qualify for an enhanced credit with no income test.

The Auditor's Homestead office is at 373 S High St, 21st Floor, Columbus, or homestead@franklincountyohio.gov. Whether you hold the exemption on the closing date decides the conveyance rate. If you think you qualify but never applied, ask the office before you set a closing date, since the timing affects what you owe.

Gahanna works as a commuter base, which helps a listing aimed at people who work elsewhere in the Columbus area. Interstate 670 and US 62 lead to John Glenn Columbus International Airport, Interstate 270 rings the area, Ohio 317 is the main north-south street through downtown, and COTA runs bus lines 24 and 25 through the center. The city uses ZIP code 43230 and sits on 12.43 square miles of land.

The Gahanna-Jefferson Public School District serves the city, and Gahanna-Lincoln is its high school. Downtown redevelopment has been part of the pitch since 2004. The Creekside project added a park extension, restaurants, offices, residences and a 389-space garage. Verify the district for your address with the county, because the Jefferson Township pockets can differ.

Properties along Big Walnut Creek, Rocky Fork Creek and Sycamore Run deserve a flood and drainage check before listing. Ask the Franklin County Auditor's office or the city for the zone of your parcel, and keep any insurance, drainage or sump-pump records handy. A documented dry basement and a clear drainage path answer the question before a buyer raises it.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Gahanna house fast
sections.html:
• Agent listing: reaches mortgage-backed buyers, who will expect a clean inspection.
  • Direct sale: no commission, but you handle the disclosure form, DTE 100 and deed paperwork.
  • Investor purchase: useful when the home needs updating, a tenant is in place or you must close on a set date.

Ohio sellers of one-to-four unit homes complete the state disclosure form. Compare offers on the amount you take home after the conveyance fee, the tax proration and any loan payoff. At the signing, bring photo identification, any payoff letter, and the lease if the house is rented. Confirm in writing who pays each closing cost before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gahanna rental that is registered with the city?
faqs.a: Yes, registration doesn't stop a sale. A buyer who keeps it as a rental registers within 30 days after the transfer, and any open violation is best cleared first.

faqs.q: How much is the Franklin County conveyance fee on a Gahanna sale?
faqs.a: Standard sales run $3 per $1,000 plus the $0.50 transfer tax, and sellers with homestead at transfer pay $1 per $1,000. Run your price through the Auditor's calculator for the exact figure.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about homestead before a Gahanna closing?
faqs.a: The Franklin County Auditor's Homestead office handles it, at 373 S High St, 21st Floor, Columbus, or homestead@franklincountyohio.gov. Whether you hold it on the closing date decides the conveyance rate.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Gahanna houses?
faqs.a: Gahanna-Jefferson Public Schools, whose high school is Gahanna-Lincoln. Small Jefferson Township pockets sit within city limits, so verify the district for your address with the county.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee when a Gahanna house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays under ORC 319.202, and the buyer files the statement of value. Your purchase contract may restate or shift it, so read the closing section.
